newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil personal credit booms in Q1 - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil personal credit booms in Q1 - cenbank.

text.p: Personal credit expanded 82.2 percent over the 12-month period to March, the Brazilian Central Bank said Monday.

The bank said in a statement that the stock of credit taken out by individuals, including overdrafts and bank loans, reached 22.204 billion reais in March compared with 12.188 billion reais in the same month a year ago.
In the first quarter of 1997, the expansion in personal credit was 12.2 percent.

The Brazilian government recently increased the tax on credit operations in a bid to slow the rapid growth in financing that was fueling an import boom and contributing to Brazil's burgeoning trade gap.
The Central Bank statement said that personal credit was the only financing sector expanding at great speed.
In first quarter 1997, the federal government reduced its credit 4.7 percent to 5.077 billion reais while the states and muncipalities expanded their credit by 4.0 percent to 56.346 billion reais.
Credit taken out by industry rose 0.7 percent to 50.94 billion, housing credit slumped 3.8 percent to 51.322 billion reais and agricultural credit increased 5.3 percent to 19.252 billion reais.
